title: Input image
what: Read from data/cleaned_1024/circuit_437.jpg.
note: If this is already a cleaned 1024 px frame, the preprocessing stages below are near no-ops. Pass --raw to trace a real photo.

title: 1. Skew estimation
what: Length-weighted median of Hough segments folded mod 90 gives +0.000°. Rejected outright if |angle| exceeds max_skew_deg.
note: A wrong angle here rotates every downstream coordinate. If the estimate is 0.000 on a visibly skewed page, Hough found too few long segments -- lower hough_min_line_frac.

title: 2. Speck removal
what: A blob survives on area OR extent, so hairline strokes are kept where a pure area rule would delete them. Red = removed.
note: Red on an actual wire means speck_min_area/extent are too aggressive; that ink is gone for the rest of the pipeline.

title: 3. Deskew, shadow-normalise, crop, scale
what: Rotated +0.00°, cropped to [3, 146, 1018, 738], scaled ×1.0059 onto a 1024 px canvas.
note: meta{} here is what project_point/unproject_point use to move GT boxes and text annotations between the photo and this canvas. If GT boxes look offset downstream, suspect this transform.

title: 4. Component detection
what: 17 boxes from cache data/detections_1024/circuit_437.json, filtered at confidence ≥ 0.4.
note: A WRONG CLASS here is the single largest remaining detection error source: the GT-class oracle is +0.0211 strict success. A spurious box is worse than a miss -- it blanks its own ink in the next stage and can sever a net.

title: 5. Text/component partition
what: 0 'Text' detections are mask evidence, never components; 17 remain as components. With a 17-class cache this is a no-op.
note: If Text boxes reached component building they would inflate benchmark alignment and be scored as circuit elements.

title: 6. Handwriting mask
what: Adaptive-threshold connected components filtered by area, aspect and size — labels like "10k" are not conductors.
note: dilate_kernel is 6, an EVEN size, so OpenCV anchors it off-centre and the mask is offset by half a pixel on both axes. Blue covering a wire means that wire is about to be deleted.

title: 7. Non-wire mask
what: Component boxes (padded by component_mask_pad) unioned with the handwriting mask. Everything red is removed from the ink.
note: component_mask_pad is 0 deliberately: at 8 it erased the wire pixels immediately next to every component -- exactly the terminals snapping then has to find -- and cost 0.163 strict success on its own. Wire Crossover is absent from non_wire_classes because masking it would sever the crossing.

title: 8. Ink binarisation
what: Otsu on the masked frame. C2: the ink itself, not Canny edges — an edge detector turns one pen stroke into TWO parallel lines with a hollow gap that morphology then has to glue back together.
note: Speckle here means the frame has low contrast; Otsu is global.

title: 9. Gap bridging
what: Line-kernel closings join stroke fragments across pen lifts. Components 21 → 13. Magenta = pixels this stage invented.
note: THE STAGE TO SUSPECT FIRST FOR WELDED NETS. A horizontal closing bridges horizontal gaps between ANY ink, so two side-by-side VERTICAL rails closer than bridge_span fuse into one conductor. That is why the span is 7 and not the 18 it shipped with. If deleted_px is non-zero the kernel is even-length and the closing is destroying ink (bridge_odd_kernel).

title: 10. Noise-blob filter
what: A blob survives on area OR extent — a hairline wire has small area but large extent, and an area-only rule shatters nets. Red = dropped.
note: Measured harmless: across 40 frames this drops 20 blobs / 623 px and NONE of them bridged two surviving components.

title: 11. Stitching across self-inflicted holes
what: Reconnects islands separated by regions OUR OWN masking deleted — text boxes and component pad rings, never a component body. Collinearity is required on both endpoints.
note: CURRENTLY INERT: with component_mask_pad=0 the pad ring is empty, so only text boxes are stitchable. Turning this off changes every topology metric by exactly 0.0000. It solved a self-inflicted problem that was later fixed at the source.

title: 12. Skeleton and intersection sites
what: Thinned centreline (black) with 50 branch sites (magenta, labelled by degree). This is where a crossing decision would be made.
note: A degree-4 site is a crossing OR a junction and the image cannot reliably tell which: six approaches on 4822 causally-labelled sites top out at 0.659 AUC, and giving the pipeline PERFECT crossover boxes makes strict success WORSE. Do not spend effort here.

title: 13. Connected components (the baseline)
what: 13 regions by plain 8-connectivity. Every crossing is welded here — this is the arrangement crossover handling has to improve on.
note: 72.6% of wire nodes carrying component terminals fuse two or more GT nets at this point.

title: 14. Net assembly (crossover)
what: 15 electrical nets, one colour each. At each detected Wire Crossover box (magenta, 2 here) the wires are notched apart and opposite arms reconnected, so a crossing does not weld two nets.
note: relink='angle' samples a ring and pairs the most-opposite arms by measured direction; 'band' votes in four fixed strips at the box edges and is placement-dependent -- a 2 px box shift once took terminal-pair F1 from 1.000 to 0.523.

title: 15. Terminal snapping (port identity)
what: Each component's pins are matched to nets. C3 assigns over DISTINCT NODES by Hungarian, not over boundary runs — the bug that fix removed was worth +0.133 per-component accuracy on its own. Yellow = snapped, red = unsnapped (0).
note: A red dot means no net was found within max_expand of that pin. Either the wire ink next to it was masked away (see stage 7) or the drawing genuinely leaves it floating.

title: 16. Constraint-triggered connectivity repair
what: Acts only where an ELECTRICAL fact makes the answer impossible: a component with every pin on one net (0.60% in GT), or a net with a single terminal (0.00% — 0 of 1509). Magenta = ink added, red = erased body band.
note: Worth +0.0211 strict success (4 gained, 0 lost) and it COMPOUNDS with connectivity work: the identical repair on the older wire settings gained only half as much, because strict success is a product over components.

title: 17. Node naming and ground selection
what: Nets are named, and one is chosen as ground (node 0) — SPICE cannot solve without a reference.
note: ground_fallback='most_connected' picks the busiest net when no GND symbol was detected. 'fail' refuses instead, which is the v2 behaviour and an ablation axis.

title: 18. SPICE netlist
what: Written to results/trace/circuit_437/netlist.sp; the repaired variant, with the repair layer's extra lines appended verbatim under a banner, is results/trace/circuit_437/netlist_repaired.sp.
note: Values are PLACEHOLDERS. The dataset ships real transcribed values, but they cannot be attached: value labels are not reliably associable with their own component (the capacitor's nearest label is often the inductor's), which was measured at 29.4% precision and a NET LOSS of 14 labels.

title: 19. Design-intent repair (C5)
what: Electrical rule checks diagnose why the circuit cannot simulate, then a minimal, fully-logged set of repairs is applied. Topology is NEVER changed here — that is stage 16's job.
note: Every entry is classified as a behaviour-invariant GAUGE choice or a flagged ASSUMPTION, so a reader can see exactly what was assumed on their behalf.

title: 20. ngspice
what: Ran netlist_repaired.sp. Result: solvable.
note: reason='timeout' would make this metric wall-clock dependent, the same defect that made nGED non-reproducible. If you see it, raise simulate.timeout_s and re-check.

title: 21. Scoring against verified ground truth
what: Strict end-to-end success requires EVERY component correct: FAIL.
note: unmatched_gt > 0 makes strict success IMPOSSIBLE for this image regardless of connectivity. per_component_exact penalises welds; per_component_recall does not and is the variant every pre-2026-07-30 result used.
